_readme: Curated golden-set labels: trend id → golden classes + why.
This file is COMMITTED on purpose — it holds the human judgement, not the content.
The scraped material itself (titles, captions, URLs, author handles) stays in
data/golden/ under .gitignore because this repository is public.
scripts/golden/curate.mjs joins these labels with the local snapshot to build
data/golden/fixtures.json. Notes describe the SIGNAL, never retell the post.
Labels are arrays: classes are not mutually exclusive (16041 is both).

16041.note: Owner-identified. Gemini set viralPattern=compilation AND described it as 'a series of humorous dog clips' — then scored 70, alertScore 69, alert fired. Owner also reports generation artefacts (unnatural motion of people, animals, furniture) that no text field captured. Primary acceptance case for the whole refactor.

16016.note: Caption opens with 'A compilation features various dogs' — pattern field said animal_action, so only the wording betrays it. Scored 65.

16014.note: viralPattern=compilation, caption 'a compilation of funny dog moments'. Scored 45 — below alert floor but still far above the 25 ceiling.

16006.note: Multi-clip cut ('transitions to different scenes of dogs') that production already scored 25. Control for the opposite error: the fix must not push correctly-handled compilations lower or destabilise them.

16066.note: Owner-identified. Generated but never pretends to be real — kittens walking upright holding paws is impossible on its face, so nobody is deceived; the AI rule must NOT crush it to zero. It must also not sit at 87: owner's verdict is that the visual is weak and overdone once you stop counting 'unusual' as merit. Dual label encodes exactly that — floor from ai_slop, ceiling from generic_animal. Gemini narrated the impossible action verbatim without concluding anything.

15861.note: Caption itself says 'An AI-generated image' — fan-art meme for a fandom, presented as art, not as evidence. Scored 65. Second negative control for the AI rule.

16153.note: No unique subject: a cat with an annoyed expression. Interchangeable with thousands. Production scored 76.

16049.note: No unique subject, no event: a dog sits and waits. Production scored 74.

16058.note: Generic pet-wakes-owner format, no named subject, no arc. Production scored 68.

15932.note: Puppy in a vest; mild framing but no distinct identity or story beyond the caption. Production scored 68.

15261.note: Celebrity-adopts-pet news. Attention is borrowed from the celebrity, not from the animal. Production scored 65.

16070.note: Distinct visual identity plus an absurd specific scene; instantly recognisable image. Production scored 88 — high score is earned.

16158.note: Owner-identified as 100% generated, presented as a real filmed moment. Initially mislabelled 'good' here — it reads as the textbook legitimate case (named subject, caught-in-the-act beat, cultural echo) and production scored 82. That is exactly why it matters: a well-made fake scores high BECAUSE it satisfies every quality signal the rubric asks for. Second acceptance case alongside 16041.

16117.note: Specific improbable-but-real scene with clear stakes and a memorable image. Production scored 79.

16065.note: Recognisable pop-culture template plus a replicable format. Production scored 77.

16144.note: Unique visual hook that is inherently shareable and remixable. Production scored 77.

16075.note: Self-defeating premise with a named protagonist — classic internet-culture shape. Production scored 80.

16068.note: Absurd but concrete personal quest with a named subject and a specific year. Production scored 78.

16156.note: Satirical escalation around a public figure; fandom-native humour. Production scored 77.

15277.note: Multi-panel format meme with an established remix template. Production scored 75.

15348.note: Quotable line from a known comic persona — travels as text alone. Production scored 75.

15482.note: Narrative thread with a genuine twist; story survives retelling. Production scored 75.

15586.note: Mundane-to-shocking pivot in one post — strong retell value. Production scored 75.

15876.note: Industry-history news item, no meme shape. Correctly scored 25 — regression guard.

16084.note: Infrastructure news, zero meme shape. Correctly scored 25 — regression guard.

16089.note: Local protest news. Correctly scored 25 — regression guard.

15774.note: Routine show-cancellation PR statement. Correctly scored 20 — regression guard.

15382.note: Routine red-carpet celebrity moment — exactly what celeb-noise filtering targets, yet production scored 55.

16130.note: google_trends, no media at all; production scored 82 purely from a search-interest signal. Tests the no-vision path against over-confidence.

15495.note: google_trends box-office item, scored 50. Mid-band no-vision behaviour.

16115.note: google_trends lottery item, scored 30 — recurring, low narrative value.

16037.note: x_trends roster transaction, scored 20. Correct low score without vision.

15991.note: x_trends roster transaction, scored 15. Floor-level case: proves a low score is allowed, which is why text_only has no lower bound.
